detail: TelegramPolicy wraps an inner Policy and only intercepts ASK; the tool's own Telegram HTTP call (send_message/poll_decision) is the mocked test boundary, not the Policy.evaluate path itself, mirroring how my-tester/my-reporter mock the gh Runner rather than internal logic

ask_human catches any transport/API exception and resolves DENY/outcome=timeout rather than propagating -- the design's fail-closed invariant applies to network errors identically to a real timeout, so both collapse to the same ledger outcome

notify reads only the shared runtime Ledger (not dev-ledger) -- it pushes live operational activity (kind=run/report/changelog/ask/drift), not per-repo build provenance; bookmark is its own last kind=notify entry's ts, entries with ts > bookmark are pushed as one combined multi-line message

implemented TelegramTransport (Protocol) + HTTPTelegramTransport (stdlib urllib.request + json, sendMessage/getUpdates long-poll, no SDK), TelegramPolicy + ask_human (fail-closed ASK relay), notify (incremental ledger push); 10 tests green, ruff clean
pushed to github.com/MyThingsLab/my-telegram-bot; PR #1 opened, CI green on first push

added a workflow_dispatch-only manual-ask-test.yml (no push/pull_request trigger, so it never fires on its own) to smoke-test TelegramPolicy end-to-end against the real Telegram API using the already-stored secrets, without ever re-handling the token locally
